correctness.rationale: The polar of the shifted unit cube is exactly an axis-intercept cross-polytope, with the explicitly computed orthant-simplex volume. The projective polar-volume Jacobian identity gives an exact expectation of a negative power over independent uniform variables. Its Hessian in the centering variables at zero is positive definite; strict polar-volume convexity identifies the analytic critical branch as the global Santaló center. An explicit fourth-moment expansion and quadratic stationarity yield the exact quadratic and quartic invariant coefficients with sixth-order analytic remainder. Reflection and permutation symmetry force an analytic symmetric function of coordinate squares; derivative differences are divisible by coordinate differences. Their leading quotient is twice the quartic anisotropy coefficient, whose cubic numerator is negative through dimension 15 and positive from dimension 16. The strict Schur criterion then gives the complete local extrema and equality classes. The included code independently verifies symbolic identities, numerical minimizers and direct integrals; these finite computations corroborate, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The source constructs related shifted-zonotope optimal regularizers but does not evaluate the Santaló product. The closest public unequal-height bipyramid theorem already gives the single-axis quadratic coefficient, which is credited, but cannot compare multiaxis deformations at fixed squared displacement. The new signed fourth-order mixed invariant and its dimension-sixteen extremal inversion require a higher-order multi-parameter calculation. General Santaló rationality, shadow systems, and the simplex-reflection product result do not imply this specific sign reversal. Relevant public research records and relevant prior public claims were compared by implications, not merely titles. Unindexed differently parametrized literature remains a risk.
residual_risks: A differently parameterized higher-order perturbation formula may exist in older convex-geometry literature without searchable terminology.
Full Meyer–Reisner 2006 article was not materially inspected beyond its abstract, so an unlocated corollary may have priority implications.
Pavlov–Telen PDF was read selectively, not exhaustively; targeted searches and stated main theorems do not settle every possible hidden specialization.

value.rationale: A natural family of asymmetric cross-polytopes arises as polars of shifted cube/zonotope regularizers. The quadratic Santaló deficit cannot distinguish allocation patterns at fixed squared imbalance; the exact mixed fourth-order invariant does, with a sharp dimension-sixteen sign reversal. This yields a mathematically motivated and complete local classification of all minimizers and maximizers rather than a substitution, isolated finite table value, or conjectural improvement. The result may guide study of multiaxis asymmetry in volume-product geometry.
